ledger.claim: The rider's case is a single number, and the driver's own trace refutes it. The fare charges SGD 3.00 for the 'AYE Alexandra Rd gantry' at lat 1.289647, lng 103.863838 (EV-FARE-02816), but of the 162 fixes in the trace the closest to that gantry is 330.73 m away, at 2026-08-30T11:10:50+08:00 (EV-GPS-02816). POL-RD-09 matches a gantry to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m of it as a crossing; 330.73 m is outside that radius, so on the only measurement the policy recognises the vehicle never crossed this gantry and the line is a phantom charge. The rider's claim that the charge is for 'a road we never used' is therefore not an assertion but a measured fact.

The 330.73 m closest approach is not an artefact of a broken or gappy trace, so it cannot be explained away. Coverage is 100.0%, the gaps array is empty, max_gap_sec is 0.0, the sampling interval is a steady 10 s against an expected 10 s, and the proximity block itself records gap_brackets_closest_approach = false with across_gap_distance_m null (EV-GPS-02816). POL-RD-07's impairment limbs - a gap over 90 seconds, a straight-line jump over 500 m, an interval above 30 seconds - are none of them met, so the trace is policy-clean and the closest approach stands exactly as measured. Both artifacts the claim rests on are COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0.

The remedy is fixed by POL-RD-09(4): a charge line for a gantry the gps_trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists, and recorded as a billing-integrity finding in the ruling's referrals list. The full SGD 3.00 charged for that line must be returned to the rider. Because it is a standalone correction and not a POL-RD-02 recomputation, it is not trimmed by the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and not netted against any distance or time figure - the rider's entitlement is the whole of the line the platform raised for a crossing that did not happen.

The rider does not need a deviation finding to be paid, and the record would not give her one. Measured on the governing field, the trace distance of 20.58 km (EV-GPS-02816 - not the rounded 20.6 km convenience copy on the trip record) against an optimal of 19.6 km (EV-TRIP-02816) yields an excess of 0.98 km, or 5.0% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to clear both 0.8 km in absolute terms and 20% of optimal, so the percentage limb fails and no deviation is established; POL-RD-02 does not run. The rider accepts that, because POL-RD-01 expressly preserves a billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4) whether or not a deviation exists. The practical consequence is favourable: since no POL-RD-02 recomputation arises, POL-RD-09(1) does not absorb the ERP correction into a recomputed fare, and the SGD 3.00 is payable on top of the fare as charged rather than swallowed by it.

This is a case the tribunal can decide today, not one that must be sent to a human with the money frozen. POL-RD-10(8) escalates where a charge line has no counterpart anywhere in the trace or trip record, but POL-RD-09(4) states expressly that POL-RD-10(8) is NOT triggered where the only unmatched line is one refunded under that limb. The AYE gantry line is the only unmatched line on this fare: off_optimal_route_total is SGD 3.00 and on_optimal_route_total is SGD 0.00, with the single line flagged on_optimal_route false (EV-FARE-02816). Every other fare component - base fare, distance, time, platform fee - has its counterpart in the trip record. The case can therefore be ruled on and the correction moved now.

Nothing said on the other side touches this finding. The only statement on file is the driver's 'The ERP is charged by the system', which names no artifact and no clause; the trip's chat log holds 0 messages, first and last message timestamps both null (EV-CHAT-02816), so no admission, correction or explanation exists in the record either. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded. That a machine raised the line rather than a person is not an answer: POL-RD-09(4) tests a gantry line against the trace, and the trace says the gantry was not crossed. The fare ledger itself does not corroborate the crossing - it simply reports the amount charged and records that the line is off the optimal route.

The bundle holds no traffic advisory that could legitimise the off-optimal corridor. EV-ADVIS-02816-01 is MISSING, carries weight_multiplier 0.0 and fired issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, the assessor recording that no advisory covers the Tampines Mall corridor in this window; under POL-GEN-02(3) a MISSING artifact carries no fact and its absence is itself citable, and under POL-GEN-02(1) I disclose that impairment expressly rather than lean on it as clean evidence. POL-RD-03 will only exonerate a deviation on an advisory that names a segment the optimal route traverses with a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle reaching it, and POL-RD-13 confines any traffic excuse to that same comparison; there is no such record here, so no advisory supports the route driven and nothing in the bundle places a valid reason under the AYE gantry line.

The rider's entitlement is not diluted by her history, and no profile can decide this point either way. POL-GEN-01 permits the profiles to inform credibility only - no profile field may establish a fact about this trip - and POL-RD-08's corroboration uplift engages only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more against 1 or fewer substantiated claims. The rider sits at 1 claim in 60 days and 0 substantiated (EV-RPROF-02816), so the uplift does not engage and the single trace measurement under POL-RD-09 is sufficient; the remaining rider and driver profile fields are context only and may ground no finding.

No route deviation exists on this trip, and the rider's pleading is not about a deviation. The governing measurement is the trace, which runs 20.58 km against a booked optimal of 19.60 km — an excess of 0.98 km, or 5.00% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires an excess to be greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km, and both tests must pass; 5.00% fails the percentage limb by a wide margin, so the excess is not a deviation however the rider characterises the trip. The trip_record agrees on its face, carrying deviation_pct of 5.0.

Because no deviation is established under POL-RD-01, POL-RD-02 never runs: there is no recomputed fare, no refund of any part of the distance charge (SGD 14.70) or the time charge (SGD 7.42), and off-route ERP is never comprehended into a distance refund. The claim on file pleads a single SGD 3.00 ERP line and asserts nothing about distance or time, so nothing in the claim reaches the distance and time lines at all.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08: matched trip identifiers and an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired trace. The only trace in the bundle is unimpaired and complete, and it shows 5.00%, so the burden is not discharged on the deviation element. The rider's own 60-day record — deviation_claims_60d of 1 with deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0 — adds nothing: POL-RD-08's reliability factor is not even met, since it requires four or more claims in 60 days to bite, and in any event that factor may never be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven.

The trace cannot be attacked for gaps: it carries 162 fixes at a 10.0 second interval against a 10.0 second expected interval, a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds and 100.0% coverage. POL-RD-07's impairment limbs (a) to (c) are therefore not met, so neither the impaired-stretch measurement rule nor the independent-corroboration requirement is engaged, and the deviation question is decided on the trace as measured — which measures no deviation. The trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown are all admissibility-COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the deciding facts carry no discount and the platform's 0.70 confidence floor is not approached under POL-GEN-02.

The rider's assertion that the vehicle 'never used' that road rests on a fix-level statistic, not on the path. The trace's nearest fix stands 330.73 m from the AYE Alexandra Rd gantry, while POL-RD-09's match rule makes a fix inside a 250 m radius a crossing and does not convert a fix outside the radius into proof that the continuous path never entered it, the sampling interval being 10 seconds. No other artifact supplies the missing proof: the chat log holds no messages, the trace carries no rider track, and no rider-side record of the gantry is in the bundle. On this record the gantry is not shown to be a line the trace never passes, and no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4) is established.

In the alternative, if the judge treats the line as unmatched, the correction is confined to the line itself. POL-RD-09(4) is a standalone billing-integrity correction of the charge as recorded, and the fare ledger itemises exactly one ERP line — AYE Alexandra Rd gantry, SGD 3.00 — against a pleaded SGD 5.00. POL-RD-09(1) and (2) have no work to do here, there being no POL-RD-02 deviation refund and no POL-RD-03 closure, and the correction is a pass-through of a government-set charge rather than a payment by the driver; the ledger is COMPLETE and reconciles to total_charged, so no other line is in issue.

The bundle holds no traffic advisory covering this trip: EV-ADVIS-02816-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and I disclose that impairment in relying on its absence. The driver has never asserted an external traffic cause — the counterparty statement is that the ERP is charged by the system — so POL-RD-03 is unavailable on the record, no closure-adjusted optimal is produced, and the absence is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it, not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation, because no party has invoked the missing identifier against a cited artifact.

Even if POL-RD-06 were consulted, no repeat-deviation pattern can be established: the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 395 completed trips in 90 days, far below both the count limb and the 0.05 ratio limb. POL-RD-06 is in any event not engaged, because POL-RD-01 records no deviation on this trip, material or otherwise, so no conduct referral and no FULL_REFUND uplift can follow from it. Every other entry on the driver's profile — rating, acceptance_rate, prior_no_show_flags, prior_deviation_flags — is context only under POL-GEN-01 and may not ground a finding against him.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver — this ruling decides DSP-02816 on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare ledger for TRP-02816.

ROUTE DEVIATION: NONE. Both sides read the trace the same way and they are right. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess exceeds 20% of the optimal distance AND 0.8 km. The governing trace figure (EV-GPS-02816, not the rounded 20.6 km convenience copy on the trip record) is 20.58 km against a booked optimal of 19.60 km (EV-TRIP-02816) — an excess of 0.98 km, or 5.00%. The percentage limb fails, so no deviation is established, POL-RD-02 does not run, and the distance charge of SGD 14.70 and the time charge of SGD 7.42 stand.

THE ERP LINE: REFUNDED IN FULL. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02816) carries one ERP line — AYE Alexandra Rd gantry, SGD 3.00, at lat 1.289647, lng 103.863838. POL-RD-09 matches a gantry to the trace by treating a fix within 250 m of it as a crossing; the nearest of the trace's 162 fixes is 330.73 m away (at 11:10:50), outside that radius. The trace is complete — 100.0% coverage, a steady 10-second interval, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c). On the measurement the policy prescribes, that gantry was not crossed. POL-RD-09(4) makes a charge for a gantry the trace never passes a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction available whether or not a deviation exists. Amount returned: SGD 3.00. The SGD 0.50 de minimis floor governs POL-RD-02 recomputations and does not trim this correction, and the correction is not netted against distance or time. The disputed amount on file is SGD 5.00, but the claim as pleaded is the SGD 3.00 ERP line and that is what is returned; base fare SGD 3.80, distance SGD 14.70, time SGD 7.42 and platform fee SGD 0.80 all reconcile to the trip record and are properly chargeable. Total charged was SGD 30.55.

ARGUMENTS THAT DID NOT SUCCEED. (1) The driver's submission that a 330.73 m closest approach does not prove the path never entered the 250 m circle is rejected: the 250 m radius is the match rule POL-RD-09 itself states, the trace is dense and gap-free, and the gantry carries coordinates, so the 'undecidable, treat as matched' rule for coordinate-less gantries does not apply. (2) The driver's alternative submission succeeds and is reflected in the remedy: the correction is confined to the single line, SGD 3.00, and is a pass-through of a government-set charge rather than a payment by the driver. (3) The driver's statement that 'the ERP is charged by the system' cites no artifact and no clause; under POL-RD-08 an assertion that points to nothing carries no weight, and that a machine raised the line does not answer POL-RD-09(4), which tests the line against the trace.

PROFILES. No profile field decides anything here. POL-GEN-01 makes rating, acceptance rate, account age, lifetime trips, cancellation rate and the lifetime prior_* counters context only, and they were not used. The citable counters were checked and neither test engages: driver deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 395 completed trips in 90 days, so POL-RD-06 finds no pattern and no conduct referral follows; rider deviation_claims_60d is 1 with 0 substantiated, so POL-RD-08's reliability factor does not bite.

MISSING ADVISORY. EV-ADVIS-02816-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) and carries no fact. No party asserted an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 was unavailable on the record and no closure-adjusted optimal exists; this is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction, and it does not escalate the case.

ESCALATION AND EXECUTION. No escalation applies. POL-RD-10(8) is expressly not triggered where the only unmatched fare line is one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), the POL-RD-09(4) referral is an addition to this ruling and not an escalation, and nothing in POL-RD-10(1)–(7) fires. Every artifact the ruling rests on is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so no POL-GEN-02(2) discount caps confidence and the 0.70 floor is not approached. The monetary effect, SGD 3.00, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold in POL-GEN-05 and is executed automatically on issue. This is a provisional ruling made without human review; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral: the AYE Alexandra Rd gantry ERP line of SGD 3.00 itemised on EV-FARE-02816 was charged for a gantry the EV-GPS-02816 trace never passes (nearest of 162 fixes 330.73 m, outside the 250 m match radius, trace complete at 100.0% coverage and a steady 10 s interval); the line is refunded as a standalone pass-through correction and the gantry charge on TRP-02816 is flagged for billing-integrity review.
